title: Kieran Trippier to leave Newcastle this summer: Does it make sense, and do they need to replace him?
content:
Kieran Trippier will leave Newcastle United when his contract expires at the end of the season.

It will bring an end to the 35-year-old’s four-and-a-half years at St. James’ Park, having joined from Atletico Madrid in January 2022.

Capped 54 times by England, Trippier has been an integral part in Eddie Howe’s side, making 157 appearances for the club and featuring in 18 Premier League matches this season.

“This is where I have felt most at home. It’s emotional, and I’m really going to miss it,” Trippier said in a statement confirming his upcoming departure.

Addressing his team-mates, Trippier said: “It’s been an amazing journey with you guys. I’m going to miss you all, but to win a trophy with you guys was really, really special – the best of my career.”

Trippier played 90 minutes as Newcastle defeated Liverpool in the 2024-25 Carabao Cup final, winning the club’s first major piece of silverware in 50 years.

Newcastle coach Howe added: “From the moment he walked through the door, he has helped to drive standards that have changed the club’s trajectory.

“His leadership skills have been invaluable. In difficult moments his experience has proved calming and his drive and will to win has inspired the players to keep pushing
forward.”

Newcastle, 12th in the Premier League, are next in action away to Crystal Palace on April 12 and Trippier’s final match will be the game at Fulham on May 24.

A graduate of Manchester City’s youth academy, Trippier helped Burnley reach the Premier League before a 2015 switch to Tottenham Hotspur, for whom he started the 2019 Champions League final. He left Spurs at the end of that season to join Atletico Madrid, where he won La Liga in 2021.

Trippier is one of the most important players in Newcastle’s modern history, the first new signing through the door post-takeover. He was a tone-setter, a standard-bearer, fresh from winning La Liga and thrust into what was, at the time, a relegation battle at St James’ Park.

He gave the club instant credibility. If the England international was prepared to make this leap, was prepared to get his hands dirty, then others will follow.

Trippier was not just a great defender, he was a leader par excellence, someone who lifted levels in the dressing room, pushing other players to rise with him. He was Howe’s on-field lieutenant, a captain even when others physically wore the armband.

Trippier’s spell on Tyneside has not always been straightforward. The arrival of the young and talented Tino Livramento in 2023 meant Trippier could see his own footballing mortality. There have been times when he has come close to leaving, something Howe never wanted for obvious reasons.

Livramento’s injury record this season has meant regular football for Trippier, who is 36 later this year. In moments of real difficulty, whether for Howe or the team, he has stepped forward, prominent on the pitch and taking responsibility off it.

His departure is not a surprise. With his contract expiring at the end of this season and given his age, it is probably the right decision for all parties.

On his day, he is still a fabulous player but in the dynamic, pacy Premier League Trippier cannot possibly have the same impact as he once did.

In the past, Newcastle have frequently held on to players for too long and the timing of this news feels right. It means a genuine Newcastle legend — standard-bearer and trophy-winner — will get a proper farewell.

Trippier will need to be replaced and there is a possibility that Newcastle will be searching for two new right-backs this summer.

Livramento only has two years remaining on his current and there has been no public communication about a possible extension.

Manchester City have been credited with an interest in the England defender and if both men were to leave it would represent a recruitment headache for Newcastle.

One thing is for certain: whoever comes after Trippier will have big boots to fill.
